name: LatentInterpolate (direction-and-magnitude blend)
plain: Core's LatentInterpolate is not a lerp or a true slerp. It normalises each latent per pixel across channels, lerps the unit directions, renormalises, then applies a lerped magnitude. This keeps per-pixel vector length at the blended magnitude rather than shrinking it as a lerp does. This per-pixel behaviour holds for a batch of 1; the norms are taken without keepdim, so larger batches fail on broadcasting (inference from the code, not run).
math:
m1=‖s1‖₂ over channel dim, m2=‖s2‖₂
u1=s1/m1, u2=s2/m2 (nan→0)
t = u1·ratio + u2·(1−ratio)
out = (t/‖t‖)·(m1·ratio + m2·(1−ratio))
ratio=1 returns samples1, ratio=0 returns samples2.
m has no kept channel dim, so this holds for batch 1 only (inference from broadcasting).
